 Jalen Brunson tallied 23 points (7-of-18 FGs, 8-of-8 FTs), four rebounds, two assists and one three-pointer in Tuesday’s win over the Bucks.
 Brunson didn’t have a great night shooting the basketball, but going 8-of-8 from the foul line gave the points tally a welcome boost. The good news for Brunson and the Knicks was that they were able to take care of the Bucks with relative ease, and the captain played just 28 minutes. The Knicks host the Cavaliers on Wednesday in what will be a far more challenging contest for the reigning NBA champs.
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Jalen Brunson tallied 31 points (12-of-25 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), six rebounds, nine assists and three three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Cavaliers. 
 As in most of the Eastern Conference Finals last spring, Brunson started slowly against the Cavaliers on Saturday. But once he got going, Cleveland couldn’t come up with an answer for the Knicks’ point guard. Brunson shot 6-of-9 from the field and 3-of-3 from the foul line in the second quarter, scoring 18 points. He finished with his third 30-point game of the season, with the first two coming in wins over the Bulls. Brunson and the Knicks play four games next week, starting with the Bucks on Tuesday. 
 Jalen Brunson

 #11 
 Jalen Brunson amassed 33 points (10-of-17 FGs, 8-of-9 FTs), two rebounds, four assists and five three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Bulls. 
 Brunson started Wednesday’s game on a tear, shooting 8-of-10 from the field and scoring 22 points in the first quarter. The point total was a career-high for a first quarter for the Knicks guard, who played 28 minutes and sat out the entire fourth quarter. Brunson’s two best performances of the season have come against the Bulls, who are in the midst of a rebuild. He’ll look to build on this effort when the Knicks visit the Cavaliers on Saturday.

 Jalen Brunson tallied 19 points (6-of-16 FGs, 3-of-6 FTs), two rebounds, six assists and four three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Nets. 
 While Brunson entered Monday averaging 25.5 points per game, his percentages have not been where fantasy managers expect them to be. Over seven games, he’s shooting 39.3 percent from the field and 73.2 percent from the foul line, which is a big reason Brunson’s current value is nowhere near his preseason ADP. He’ll look to clean things up a bit on Wednesday against the Bulls.

 Coming off his most efficient performance of the season in Wednesday’s win over the Bulls, Brunson cooled off against the 76ers. Given the gap between Philadelphia and Chicago, that isn’t too surprising. However, Brunson is shooting 39.5 percent from the field through six games, which is a big reason his current fantasy value isn’t matching preseason expectations.

 Jalen Brunson tallied 38 points (13-of-25 FGs, 6-of-8 FTs), one rebound, seven assists, two steals and six three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Bulls. 
 After shooting 36.6 percent from the field in New York’s first four games, Brunson snapped out of that funk on Wednesday. Shooting 52 percent from the field and 6-of-10 from beyond the arc, the Knicks point guard finished with season highs in points, assists, steals and three-pointers. Despite the Knicks not arriving in Chicago until about 2 AM Wednesday, Brunson delivered an impressive showing.

 Jalen Brunson recorded 23 points (5-of-18 FGs, 13-of-16 FTs), one rebound and seven assists in Tuesday’s win over the Pistons. 
 Ausar Thompson hounded Brunson for most of the night, which contributed to the low field-goal percentage. A busy night at the foul line boosted the point total, and the Knicks guard dished out seven assists, so Brunson gave fantasy managers some value on Tuesday. He’ll look to bounce back on Wednesday against the Bulls.

 Jalen Brunson produced 28 points (12-of-28 FGs, 3-of-6 FTs), three rebounds, four assists, two steals, one block and one three-pointer in Sunday’s loss to the Magic. 
 Brunson led all scorers with 28 points, but the Magic made him work for every shot that he took. The Knicks’ point guard needed 28 field-goal attempts to reach that total, and he made 1-of-7 from beyond the arc. As a team, New York shot 9-of-38 from three while Orlando was 18-of-42. Essentially, that was the ballgame. Brunson has been inefficient as a scorer so far, and things won’t get any easier for him when the Pistons visit MSG on Tuesday.

 Jalen Brunson accumulated 19 points (7-of-17 FGs, 3-of-6 FTs), two rebounds, four assists, two blocks and two three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Celtics. 
 Brunson’s gotten off to a slow start by his standards, shooting 13-of-32 from the field in New York’s first two games. The Knicks star also didn’t shoot well from the foul line, missing three of his six attempts in Boston. Those rostering Brunson don’t have much to worry about, as the season is only two games old. However, they would certainly like to see him clean up his shooting in Sunday’s game against the Magic.

 Jalen Brunson led the Knicks with 21 points (6-of-19 FGs, 8-of-8 FTs), five rebounds, three assists and one three-pointer in a 106-100 loss to the 76ers on Tuesday. 
 It was a rough shooting night for Brunson, and he wasn’t able to capture the same late-game magic that brought the Knicks a championship last season. 15 of his 21 points came in the first half, but he shot just 2-of-10 from the floor after the break. He’ll be much better than he was in this game moving forward, and he’ll continue to be the focal point of the offense.

 Jalen Brunson had 20 points (7-of-15 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), three rebounds, seven assists, one steal and one three-pointer in the exhibition against the Raptors on Tuesday. 
 Brunson was back in the lineup after skipping Tuesday’s matchup against the Raptors, which was the second night of a preseason back-to-back. The 30-year-old point guard led the Knicks with 20 points in the 122-120 victory. Brunson has averaged at least 26 points in each of the last three years, making him a rock solid pick late in the second round of fantasy drafts.

 LeBron James amassed 11 points (4-of-12 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), eight rebounds, five assists and one three-pointer in Tuesday’s loss to the Celtics.
 James, who was inadvertently raked across the face by Paul George early in the fourth quarter, struggled against the Celtics. The good news for fantasy managers is that he committed just one turnover, but the 41-year-old shot the ball poorly. James, who entered Tuesday’s game shooting 25 percent from three, made just one of six three-point attempts. With the 76ers counting on Tyrese Maxey to be their lead scoring option, James’ ability to hit perimeter shots takes on added importance, and he’s struggling right now.
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Joel Embiid (foot) recorded 16 points (2-of-9 FGs, 11-of-13 FTs), six rebounds, one assist and one three-pointer in Tuesday’s loss to the Celtics.
 Given the current state of Philadelphia’s center rotation, it’s been tough for Embiid to get the break he clearly needs. The former MVP has been playing through a left foot issue that he appeared to aggravate during the third quarter. And if not for an 11-of-13 night at the foul line, Embiid’s final stat line would have looked a lot worse. After Thursday’s game against the Raptors, the 76ers have a back-to-back on Sunday and Monday, hosting the Pacers before visiting the Nets. That could be a spot where the 76ers look to rest Embiid, if possible.
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Jaylen Brown accounted for 13 points (4-of-9 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), five rebounds, two assists, two steals, one block and one three-pointer in Tuesday’s loss to the Celtics.
 Much was made of the showdown between Brown and Jayson Tatum, the first time the former teammates would face off in a regular-season game. JB struggled, landing in foul trouble in the first half and never really finding an offensive groove. Brown finished with a complete stat line, but four turnovers did fantasy managers no favors. He’ll look to bounce back on Thursday when the 76ers face the Raptors.

 Tyrese Maxey tallied 24 points (8-of-12 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), one rebound, four assists and three three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Celtics.
 Maxey had another efficient outing for the 76ers on Tuesday, shooting 66.7 percent from the field while committing just two turnovers. Unfortunately for him and the 76ers, he didn’t get much help from the other starters, with none scoring more than Joel Embiid’s 16 points. And on a night when Boston’s Paul George and Jayson Tatum combined to score 57, it’s tough to come out with the win. As expected, Maxey has provided first-round fantasy value, and he’ll look to continue on Thursday against the Raptors.
